claims.text: A machine-learned interatomic potential trained on diverse ab initio high-temperature liquid configurations will provide better reference–target phase-space overlap than standard EAM potentials.
The machine-learned reference will reduce thermodynamic-integration path mismatch relative to EAM references.
The proposed method applies to both solid and liquid multicomponent high-entropy alloys at temperatures up to approximately 1.2 Tm.
Training should cover broad liquid configurations, including near-critical fluctuations, as well as near-melting solid configurations.
The applicable alloys have two or more principal elements.
Ab initio training configurations should span multiple temperatures from above 0.8 Tm through approximately 1.2 Tm.
A flexible machine-learning potential can accurately reproduce short-range and medium-range order in the high-temperature liquid and transition configurations.
Sampling ab initio liquid configurations allows the potential to represent complex local bonding and disorder.
Representing complex local bonding and disorder yields a more faithful free-energy landscape.
A more faithful free-energy landscape improves thermodynamic-integration accuracy relative to EAM.
The intervention will decrease free-energy integration path mismatch by approximately 10–30% relative to EAM-based TOR-TILD references.
Standard EAM references have limited configurational fidelity in disordered high-temperature regimes.
The method is applicable when representative ab initio liquid and near-melting configurations can be generated for the target alloy.
Performance is less certain outside the training domain and in systems with large chemical or structural inhomogeneity.
The accuracy gain depends on the quality and breadth of the ab initio training data and may vary with composition and temperature.

The decisive benchmark is a comparison of ML-reference and EAM-reference free-energy discrepancies against direct ab initio thermodynamic integration for representative near-melting solids and liquids.
Failure to achieve the predicted 10–30% mismatch reduction, or failure to reproduce ab initio liquid structural features, falsifies the hypothesis.
